title: Global derived Hom preserves derived inverse limits on ringed sites
statement:
Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a small ringed site, with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and module category and unbounded derived category as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring with a specified homomorphism $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$. For $E,N\in D(\mathcal O)$ set
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(E,N)=R\Gamma(\mathcal C,R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(E,N))\in D(A),$$
where internal derived Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and $R\Gamma$ is the unbounded right derived functor of global sections [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] with restriction of scalars to $A$. Fix $E$ and let $(N_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a strict tower of complexes of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves. Use a resolution in the category of towers to choose the derived inverse limits; their underlying objects have the Roos triangle of [def-weil-derived-limit]. Then the canonical comparison is a natural isomorphism in $D(A)$,
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(E,R\varprojlim_nN_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_nR\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(E,N_n).$$
The comparison is induced by the projections of the strict tower, is compatible with its resolution-derived limiting cone, and is natural for maps of strict towers. No quasi-coherence of $N_n$ or of their derived limit is required. For every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ there are natural identifications $H^qR\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(E,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(E,N[q])$ for all $q\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Use the A-linear coefficient model to obtain β natural on K-injective targets and the natural A-linear cohomology equivalences.

The module-sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian. Left adjoints to evaluation applied to a separator form a separating family for towers; filtered colimits are exact levelwise. Apply the canonical functorial K-injective replacement of a tower complex; its terms are injective, so it is a resolved tower and the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Evaluation has an exact left adjoint and preserves K-injectivity. Inverse limit is right adjoint to the exact constant-tower functor, so it preserves K-injectives too. The limit of the evaluated tower is isomorphic to the degreewise inverse-limit complex, proving the K-injectivity needed to apply β. All of these steps are proved in the item by private generic helpers.
Use the resolved-tower ordinary-limit models to obtain invertibility of limit.post and the two projection-normalized Roos triangles.

At I define α_I=β_(lim I)^(-1) followed by Q(limit.post). Naturality of β applied to lim of a tower map, and the identity H(lim u)·limit.post=limit.post·lim(Hu), show this family is natural. Each component is invertible, so it is a natural isomorphism.

For each n, limit.post followed by the nth limit projection is H of the original projection. Localize this equation, apply naturality of β to the projection lim I→I_n, and cancel β_(lim I) with its inverse. This proves the asserted projection compatibility. Combine this with the two Roos triangles, resolutions, and the cohomology equivalences, without changing any conclusion.
